SPARC: 18 TF coils; historical individual coil mass ~18,025 kg (winding pack ~7,975 kg, implied non-winding-pack mass ~10,050 kg); approximately 270 km REBCO per coil across 16 pancakes; operating current ~31.3 kA; peak field ~23 T; stored energy ~316 MJ; a later completed magnet approximately 24 tonnes; first pancake cycle ~30 days, later cycle ~12 days, later target/achievement approximately 1/day; 288 pancakes total; magnet factory ~165,000 sq ft.
Fujikura invested in CFS in 2025 and expanded capacity in 2026. Faraday Factory Japan was also identified as a SPARC supplier.

SIMIC selected as main supplier for SPARC TF cases; production began July 2024; first two shipped December 10, 2024; an additional 24 cases followed, with final cases delivered in 2025. No public contract value established. Each case involves a Nitronic 50 trough, cover, SS316LN seal plate, Inconel 718 bolts, large precision forgings, and cryogenic high-strength requirements (~1 GPa stress environment): historical trough forging ~18,177 kg, cover forging ~6,697 kg, cross-section >350 mm, yield >1,200 MPa at 20 K, fracture toughness >200 MPa*m^0.5 at 77 K.

A.L.M.T./Sumitomo won an approximately ¥3.5B ITER tungsten monoblock contract in 2021; A.L.M.T.'s production capacity line expanded more than 8x; A.L.M.T. and a Chinese supplier reportedly produced approximately 65,000 monoblocks since October 2022, approximately half associated with A.L.M.T.
2026 commentary indicates tight tungsten supply and higher prices from Plansee.

ARC V3A published/current design parameters (subject to change; final material choices not frozen): major radius R0 4.62 m; minor radius a 1.18 m; plasma volume 189 m3; plasma surface area 257 m2; toroidal field B0 11.4 T; plasma current 12 MA; fusion power ~1.13 GW (performance estimates range ~600-1300 MW depending on assumptions); net electric power >=400 MW; Q ~51; 18 TF coils; max coupled RF power 50 MW (ICRF is the sole auxiliary heating system); pulse flattop ~900 s; target lifetime ~20 years; vacuum vessel replacement approximately every 1-2 full-power-years; first wall 5 mm tungsten baseline; inner wall 1 cm vanadium baseline; FLiBe cooling channel 4.5 cm; outer wall 3 cm vanadium; tungsten-carbide shielding; FLiBe used for breeding/neutron multiplication/cooling/shielding; vessel designed to be consumable/demountable; double-null long-legged X-point divertor geometry. Particularly uncertain: exact final tungsten BOM, final HTS split between TF/PF/CS, final vanadium quantity, final FLiBe quantity, tungsten-carbide shield quantity, final divertor configuration, final supplier selection, commercial procurement strategy.

Estimated total ARC REBCO: approximately 15,000-20,000 km, central working estimate 20,000 km. Not a final procurement BOM. Historical SPARC benchmark: TF system previously associated with approximately 5,730 km of REBCO in an earlier design context (extrapolation to ARC is NOT a factual ARC specification); a historical-fraction scenario would put ~9,720 km as TF-associated if ARC retained a similar TF fraction to historical SPARC. Illustrative raw tape cost $15-30/m implies $300M-$600M for 20,000 km — a cost sensitivity, not a procurement forecast. Alternative literature pricing discussed: ~$20/m competitive price, or ~$20-80/m depending on normalization. A more relevant metric for high-field conductor economics is $/kA*m: indicative current values ~$100-200/kA*m, with longer-term targets ~$10-20/kA*m.

Illustrative TF case economics (OUR_ESTIMATE / LOW_CONFIDENCE, not an observed contract price): working model $1M-$4M per case, central assumption $2M/case; 18 cases implies $18M-$72M, central ~$36M. Potential TF case supplier landscape beyond SIMIC includes MHI, HD Hyundai, Walter Tosto, CNIM, ATI, and Carpenter — none established as SPARC/ARC suppliers by evidence in this dataset.

Historical (2015) ARC Inconel vessel design: ~86.5 tonnes; fabrication estimate ~$92M (FY2014). Approximate breakdown: first wall 3.72 t / $4M; inner wall 16.6 t / $18M; outer wall 51.4 t / $55M; ribbing 6.8 t / $7.2M; posts 4.14 t / $4.4M — approximate fabrication intensity ~$1.06M/tonne. This is a historical engineering model; do not use as current ARC pricing without adjustment (materials and design have since shifted to a vanadium/tungsten baseline).
A 2025 ARC-class vessel model using V-4Cr-4Ti (density ~6.05 g/cm3) over a ~3.5 m3 vessel volume implies structural mass ~21.2 tonnes. Not the current V3A final bill of materials.

"Degradation of Electrical Resistivity of Tungsten Following Shielded Neutron Irradiation": tungsten irradiated at ORNL HFIR (~0.2-0.7 dpa, ~500-1000C) shows radiation defects degrading electron mobility/thermal transport; defect clusters and W->Re->Os transmutation both contribute (estimated ~0.83 at% Re/dpa in the relevant regime); at ~0.4 dpa/~590C defects dominate, at ~0.7 dpa/~750C Re solid-solution contribution becomes important; recrystallization occurs near ~990C. Potential mitigations: W-Re alloys, improved materials, alternative PFC materials.

A 2025 fleet study modeled large-scale tungsten demand: ARIES-ST at 500 MWth ~4,231 t, at 2 GWth ~29,034 t; EU-DEMO1 at 500 MWth ~3,945 t, at 2 GWth ~9,554 t. A large commercial fusion fleet could require very large tungsten inventories; the study indicated new tungsten resources potentially needed by ~2050, depending on deployment trajectory.
2024 world rhenium production ~62,000 kg; rhenium is mostly produced as a byproduct of copper/molybdenum mining.

ELMT announced a definitive agreement to acquire ams OSRAM's tungsten/molybdenum manufacturing operations in Schwabmünchen, Germany (powder, rods, wire, electrodes, machined components, integrated production, materials laboratory); expected closing Q1 2027. Metal-production operations have existed at the Schwabmünchen site since approximately 1961, over a production area of approximately 26,800 m2, producing more than 3,500 products with an integrated manufacturing chain (powder formation, pressing, sintering, swaging, wire drawing, finishing) plus downstream machining and powder-injection-molding capabilities and an on-site chemical/physical materials laboratory. ELMT intends to retain the existing Schwabmünchen leadership/operating team; invest in workforce, equipment, capacity, quality systems, and commercial infrastructure; support existing customers through production/transition arrangements; establish a European manufacturing platform using the site (ELMT's first EU refractory-metals manufacturing footprint, tungsten being an EU critical raw material with limited European processing capacity); and expand the material portfolio to include TZM and tungsten heavy alloy (a planned, not current, capability). Potentially increases ELMT's European manufacturing footprint, tungsten capacity, vertical integration, and geographic diversification, and explicitly identifies fusion/high-energy research as a target market for the acquired operation. This is NOT automatically fusion-positive — it could strengthen the base business independently of fusion — and does NOT establish that ELMT is currently a commercial fusion supplier.

"Neutronic analysis of tritium breeding characteristics and the neutron coupling effect in the CFETR Helium-Cooled Ceramic Breeder blanket": blanket geometry determines tritium breeding; material/structure choices matter; local under-breeding and under-multiplication can occur; whole-reactor neutron coupling matters — TBR is a system-level design problem, not a local one.

FLARE (a liquid-lithium blanket concept, blanket depth ~2m) reported TBR ~1.8, with some simulations >1.8 and one MCNP geometry ~2.06. One scenario: ~41.3 mg tritium produced/shot, ~86.8 kg/year produced, ~42.1 kg/year consumed. High TBR does not by itself prove tritium extraction, processing, containment, maintenance, reliability, or commercial economics; potential risks include vacuum integrity, corrosion, pumping, and heat removal. Core principle: TBR alone is insufficient.

source.name: Environmental Impact Assessment Review 122 (January 2027) 108654; Nuclear Fusion 63 (2023), DOI 10.1088/1741-4326/acbec7

evidence.description: Tritium extraction LCA compared four approaches (Maroni oxidation, Maroni electrolysis, direct lithium/tritium electrolysis, distillation), finding large differences in climate impact, energy use, and material requirements, driven mainly by electricity, process configuration, and system boundaries. A companion PbLi extraction study found continuous inline tritium removal important: slow extraction increases inventory, startup requirements, buffer requirements, and safety risk (methods: free surface, permeable membrane; critical variables: flow, geometry, membrane properties, diffusion, recombination). Useful framework: Net T availability = TBR x extraction efficiency x recovery efficiency - decay - leakage - inventory losses.

Tritium supply/demand study: peak theoretical stockpiles ~35.1-47.5 kg vs. ITER requirement ~15.9 kg; potential deficits under high-demand/low-supply scenarios (>28 kg shortage mid-2050s, ~42 kg by 2070, ~181 kg if reactors need ~10% external top-up; ~760 tonnes/year if fusion supplies 10% of global electricity by 2100 — highly scenario-dependent). Approximate startup tritium inventories: ITER 15.9 kg, EU-DEMO 15 kg, J-DEMO 11.25 kg, STEP 7 kg, CFEDR 3.21 kg, ARC 1.14 kg, SPARC 0.75 kg, BEST 0.89 kg. Separately, Abdou (2021) establishes TBR_A >= TBR_R as the core self-sufficiency criterion, with achievable TBR ~1.05-1.15; self-sufficiency may be possible if fueling x burn fraction > ~0.7% and processing < ~4 hours (a stronger regime: >~2% and ~1-4 hours), with example startup inventories ~11 kg for 3 GW at 2%/4h, <5 kg at 5%/1h. Startup-inventory bottlenecks are distinct from mature-fleet self-sufficiency bottlenecks.

Plasma-facing-component materials research: 2025 findings show CuCrZr precipitate coarsening causing ~29% strength loss, with a cyclic-heating model producing ~44% degradation (degradation is not simply representable as dpa). 2021 DEMO divertor findings show high uncertainty in tungsten lifetime, CuCrZr lifetime, heat flux, fatigue, ratcheting, and irradiation effects — full fusion-relevant verification remains difficult. A 2026 European material downselection considers K-doped tungsten, W2C, ZrC, WfW, ODS-Cu, and Wf-CuCr, with fabrication/high-temperature-strength/scale-up/qualification as the main challenges; COMPASS-U uses 100% tungsten coverage; 2026 K-doped tungsten mockups reached cyclic tests up to ~2000 cycles at heat flux up to ~20 MW/m2, with qualification ongoing.

Maintenance/availability research: Crofts & Harman (2014) found blanket/divertor sector replacement around every ~1000h, with four remote-handling systems considered for ~75% availability; Farquhar (2019) modeled planned in-vessel maintenance <=250 days (e.g. 30 days cooldown, 30 days pumpdown/conditioning), with blanket replacement estimates ranging 825 days (1 RM system) down to 155 days (6 systems), and laser cutting/welding improvements saving ~180h/sector and cutting welding from 70h to 29h. Schwartz (2026) found plant value can be ~15% higher than naive availability-proportional calculations, that 80% availability with annual maintenance can retain ~91% of plant value, that maintenance timing matters, and modeled blanket durability ~0.7-5 FPY with blanket cost ~$0-500M/GW. Tesini (2026) proposed a "Q_ENG" engineering burden index cascading from Q_PHYSICS through Q_ENG, Q_GLOBAL, to Q_PLANT.

Almonty's Sangdong tungsten processing began July 2026. An amended offtake with GTP/Plansee runs approximately 21 years, approximately 4.41M MTU, with volume increased ~40% and improved pricing. Fusion demand is only one possible demand source; current economics are driven by broader tungsten market conditions.

evidence.description: Asset Purchase Agreement dated 2026-09-03: ELMT's newly formed German subsidiary, Elmet Technologies GmbH, agreed to acquire assets and rights associated with the Schwabmünchen operation from ams OSRAM/OSRAM GmbH via an asset purchase. Approximately 157 employees were associated with the relevant metal-production business at the time of the transaction documentation, with planned workforce restructuring following the transaction. Existing customers are intended to be supported through production/transition arrangements; ELMT will assume supply, quality, and technical support responsibilities for the transferred business after closing. The purchase-price mechanism is a formula beginning with a negative EUR 18M amount, then adjusted for items including pension assets, defined-benefit pension liabilities, a restructuring prepayment, working capital relative to a specified target, and other transaction-specific adjustments — the final closing consideration is NOT simply "ELMT paid/received EUR 18M" and remains UNKNOWN until closing.

Historical OSRAM materials documentation indicates the Schwabmünchen operation's experience with multiple tungsten compositions (including pure tungsten and potassium-doped tungsten), molybdenum products, an integrated manufacturing chain (powder formation, pressing, sintering, swaging, wire drawing, finishing), and downstream machining/powder-injection-molding capabilities, plus chemical/physical materials-analysis capabilities. Does not establish current commercial production volumes.

A documented publication involving personnel associated with the Schwabmünchen/ams OSRAM operation concerns tungsten wire/materials research for fusion-reactor applications. This establishes historical fusion-materials technical research involvement. It does NOT establish commercial fusion supply, ITER/DEMO/private-fusion qualification, a fusion customer relationship, or fleet-scale fusion supply.

Freemelt AB announced it received an order from Fusion for Energy (F4E) to manufacture and deliver 33,000 tungsten-based components for the JT-60SA fusion programme. The order has a base value of SEK 55 million (approximately €5 million) and a potential total value of up to SEK 84 million (approximately €7.5 million). Deliveries are expected over two years through 2028, with the majority scheduled for 2027, to JT-60SA in Japan.

Fujikura's disclosure states it has had a relationship with Commonwealth Fusion Systems since CFS's founding and has been supplying HTS wire to CFS, and that it is making additional capital investments to increase HTS production for fusion-energy reactors.

UKAEA reported £40M of FOSTER funding supporting fusion education and training, including new Master's programs.
CFS raised another $1B, bringing total capital raised to $4B.
Syntec reported new fusion orders worth seven times its late-2025 order volume for specialized fusion optics; customer(s) undisclosed.
ORNL licensed four cryogenic pellet-fueling inventions to Type One Energy.
TAE and Black Moon Energy signed an agreement establishing a prospective helium-3 supply option — a supply OPTION, not a current qualified/active supply relationship.
UKAEA completed the fifth MAST Upgrade experimental campaign with record plasma performance.
UKAEA restarted the Materials Detritiation Facility following a 12-month engineering upgrade.
DOE committed funding for UNITY-3, a fusion breeding-blanket test facility at ORNL, developed with Kyoto Fusioneering.
UKAEA spun out Singular Machines with strategic investment and a new Arup contract for the coEngen engineering-automation platform (general engineering, not fusion-specific).
Thea Energy extended its Series B financing to support magnet manufacturing, Eos and Helios.
Inertia reported reducing fusion fuel-pellet production from days to hours (company-reported figure).
Kyoto Fusioneering secured ¥16.72B equity plus ¥9B credit and loan facilities.
NNSA and Pacific Fusion signed an MOU for high-yield fusion and high-energy-density science collaboration.
Pacific Fusion broke ground on its Research and Manufacturing Campus in Albuquerque.
UKAEA began an asset-based decommissioning trial with Ramco.
Tennessee issued Type One Energy the state's first fusion-specific byproduct-material license.

UKAEA (trading as UK Fusion Energy Limited) issued an open procurement notice seeking to progress the design and manufacturability of a novel transmission system planned for integration into the MAST Upgrade (MAST-U) EBW transmission line, including microwave tubes, microwave equipment, and associated engineering design. This is an open procurement opportunity, not an awarded contract.

ITER reported continued assembly progress: installation of two additional toroidal field coils in sector module 9, completion of the vacuum-vessel thermal-shield repair program, the start of bellows-system installation, transfer of another vacuum-vessel sector onto its gravity support, and preparation of sector 3 for assembly. These are worksite construction/assembly activities; no new supplier contract or commercial qualification is established by this update.

SSEN Transmission signed a long-term framework agreement with a Sumitomo Electric and Van Oord consortium for engineering, supply, transport, and installation of HVDC subsea cable systems in the north of Scotland, intended to support future strategic transmission reinforcements including the proposed Shetland 2 HVDC link. This is an HVDC power-cable framework agreement (not the superconducting-cable line of business specifically); a framework, with a specific call-off contract still to follow.

General Fusion completed its business combination with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III and began trading on Nasdaq under ticker GFUZ, becoming the first publicly listed fusion power company; shares rallied roughly 40% from the opening price of $12.85.

Syntec Optics announced a new recurring space order, described as expanding its footprint from 'orbital highway' components to 'critical orbital safety' applications. Specific counterparty not disclosed.

American Superconductor (AMSC) announced a $25 million contract to supply a turnkey power quality solution (STATCOM technology, capacitor banks, shunt reactors, a 138kV transformer, switchgear, and controls) to a North American utility supporting a major mining project — described as the largest single order in company history tied to mining development. Specific utility/mining customer not named in the coverage reviewed.
Kennametal reported fiscal 2026 and fourth-quarter results, with Q4 sales of $737 million (up 43% organically) and record adjusted EPS of $2.96.

Furukawa Electric issued a notice regarding acquisition of fixed assets for the production of optical fibers and optical fiber cables. This facility investment is in optical fiber/cable production, not the tracked HTS-wire business specifically.

Furukawa Electric reported Q1 FY ending March 2027 results: net sales up 24.3% YoY to ¥365.2 billion, operating profit up 205.4% to ¥25.5 billion, driven partly by strong data center demand; the company raised its full-year consolidated forecast. General financial results, not specific to the HTS-wire business.

Fujikura Ltd. reported Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) results: sales of ¥402,009 million (vs ¥267,908 million a year earlier) and net income of ¥80,434 million (vs ¥31,318 million), driven primarily by optical fiber cable and data center demand. Results reporting did not specifically reference the HTS/superconducting-wire business.

The Elmet Group Co. reported Q2 2026 results: firm order backlog grew to approximately $131.5 million (up from ~$113.3M at end of Q1 2026 and ~$84.6M at end of Q2 2025), with the aerospace/defense/government backlog segment up over 100% year-over-year on new missile system, radar, and aerospace program awards.

Almonty Industries reported Q2 2026 (three and six months ended June 30, 2026) financial results: revenue increased 498% year-over-year to $43.0 million, net income of $181.8 million (vs a loss of $58.2 million in Q2 2025), and cash of $1.23 billion as of June 30, 2026 (up from $268.4 million at Dec 31, 2025), following an $800 million convertible senior notes offering that closed June 9, 2026 (outside this evidence window; only the resulting cash position, disclosed in this Q2 report, falls within it).

Freemelt disclosed (in its Q2 2026 interim report) an additional order from Saab Dynamics for a Phase II application-test project to manufacture copper components for defense-industry additive manufacturing, following an earlier feasibility study. Prospective/qualification-stage work, not yet serial production.

General Fusion issued its first public-company business update, reporting approximately $150 million in cash to fund its Lawson Machine 26 (LM26) program through planned technical milestones to end of 2028, plasma heating of about 0.72 keV (8.4 million °C) using a lithium liner, a milestone-based framework agreement with Renexia S.p.A. for potential deployment in Italy, and a collaboration with General Atomics Energy Group on plasma diagnostics. The Renexia agreement is milestone-based/framework, i.e. prospective, not a firm deployment contract.

Kennametal announced the election of Dawne S. Hickton and Richard J. Harshman to its Board of Directors, and the appointment of Joseph Alvarado as incoming Chairman of the Board effective October 28, 2026.
Syntec Optics announced it won a new recurring space order as the space economy expands, including specialized high-tech waveguides for space satellites moving into weekly production.

Jefferies Financial Group initiated equity research coverage of Almonty Industries with a Buy rating and a $26.25 price target, around the same time as the formal removal of Almonty's CHESS Depositary Interests from the Australian Securities Exchange. This is sell-side analyst opinion, not a corporate action by Almonty itself.
General Fusion announced it would participate in upcoming investor conferences. Administrative/IR announcement, minimal substantive content.

Syntec Optics announced it secured $5 million in additional recurring orders for a diverse range of U.S. defense platforms, including optics used in missile guidance, which grew roughly 30% since a prior increase.

assertions.statement: Supplier qualification does not imply commercial procurement.
Specialized manufacturing capability can create supplier switching costs.
A fusion stock rising because fusion headlines are positive does not imply future earnings increase.
A company saying "we work in fusion" may have less economic exposure to fusion than a boring industrial supplier does.
Selling a fusion-relevant commodity material does not necessarily mean capturing fusion economics.
Being technically capable of manufacturing a component does not imply being qualified to supply it for fusion.
One prototype or demonstration-scale contract does not imply fleet-scale commercial revenue.
A large company receiving modest fusion revenue may have less fusion economic leverage than a much smaller company receiving less absolute fusion revenue.

The most economically attractive supplier may not be the one selling the most material, but the one controlling the component whose absence stops the reactor; bottleneck power should be modeled independently of revenue size.

A component with a high replacement frequency can have greater lifetime economics than a component with a large one-time sale; fleet economic exposure is initial deployment demand plus replacement demand.

hypotheses.name: T-001
hypotheses.statement: Tungsten becomes a fusion materials bottleneck.

hypotheses.name: T-002
hypotheses.statement: Rhenium becomes a meaningful bottleneck.

assessments.rationale: Lower conviction than the primary tungsten bottleneck.

hypotheses.name: T-003
hypotheses.statement: Tritium self-sufficiency is a major reactor-design constraint.

assessments.rationale: Source estimate range ~0.75-0.90; 0.82 recorded as the point estimate.

hypotheses.name: T-008
hypotheses.statement: Tritium availability may constrain industry growth.

hypotheses.name: T-009
hypotheses.statement: High-TBR reactors have strategic value because of tritium surplus.

hypotheses.name: H016
hypotheses.statement: Raw HTS scarcity may become a bottleneck but is not necessarily the ultimate bottleneck.

hypotheses.name: H018
hypotheses.statement: Qualified high-field conductor manufacturing is a bigger bottleneck than raw tape supply.

hypotheses.name: H019
hypotheses.statement: TF consumes the majority of ARC HTS.

assessments.rationale: Uncertainty is high because the V3A TF/PF/CS split is not publicly finalized.

hypotheses.name: H020
hypotheses.statement: Value migrates downstream from raw tape toward conductor/magnet integration.

hypotheses.name: H021
hypotheses.statement: Qualified kA*m is a more economically meaningful unit than raw km of HTS tape.

hypotheses.name: H022
hypotheses.statement: CFS captures a larger share of downstream HTS value than raw-tape suppliers do.

hypotheses.name: H023
hypotheses.statement: Magnet manufacturing is a commercialization bottleneck.

hypotheses.name: H024
hypotheses.statement: Integrated magnet manufacturing captures more value than raw tape production.

hypotheses.name: H026
hypotheses.statement: Learning curves materially reduce magnet/conductor costs over time.

assessments.rationale: SPARC pancake-winding cycle time fell from ~30 days to a ~1/day target/achievement.

hypotheses.name: H032
hypotheses.statement: Vacuum-vessel fabrication is a major commercial bottleneck.

assessments.rationale: Only one vessel fabricator has demonstrated qualification-track progress.
Qualification achieved; no second fabricator has emerged.
No competing vessel fabricator has qualified after two additional years.

falsifiers.description: A second, independently qualified vacuum-vessel fabricator emerges.

hypotheses.name: H033
hypotheses.statement: Vessel qualification creates switching costs.

assessments.rationale: Qualification represents a multi-year, capital-intensive process few competitors have replicated.
CFS has not re-qualified an alternate vessel fabricator.

falsifiers.description: SPARC re-bids vessel-adjacent work to a new entrant without measurable switching cost.

hypotheses.name: H034
hypotheses.statement: SPARC suppliers have informational/procurement advantages for later commercial orders.

assessments.rationale: Demonstration-scale suppliers plausibly carry forward institutional knowledge.
Continued reliance on the same qualified suppliers through the demonstration program.

falsifiers.description: A supplier with no SPARC history wins a comparable commercial contract on equal footing.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-001
hypotheses.statement: Schwabmünchen materially increases ELMT's tungsten/molybdenum manufacturing capacity.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-002
hypotheses.statement: Schwabmünchen provides ELMT with vertically integrated refractory-metals manufacturing capabilities that complement its existing U.S. operations.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-003
hypotheses.statement: The acquisition provides ELMT with meaningful European tungsten manufacturing capability.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-004
hypotheses.statement: The Schwabmünchen operation possesses pre-existing technical expertise relevant to fusion materials.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-005
hypotheses.statement: The Schwabmünchen operation's existing capabilities could potentially be adapted for commercial fusion-material production.

assessments.rationale: This is an inference and should remain explicitly labeled as such (source_type: INFERENCE).

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-006
hypotheses.statement: ELMT could obtain qualification for at least one fusion-material application.

assessments.rationale: Intentionally conservative because qualification evidence is currently insufficient.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-007
hypotheses.statement: The acquisition increases ELMT's long-term exposure to fusion-material demand.

hypotheses.name: H-ELMT-008
hypotheses.statement: The acquisition could eventually allow ELMT to participate in recurring tungsten replacement demand from commercial fusion reactors.

assessments.rationale: Highly speculative until qualification and customer evidence exists.

models.name: Fusion Revenue Model
models.description: Fusion Revenue = Reactors Deployed x Component Content per Reactor x Supplier Market Share x Replacement Count

calculations.name: Fusion Revenue
calculations.formula: Fusion Revenue = Reactors Deployed x Component Content per Reactor x Supplier Market Share x Replacement Count

models.name: ARC First-Wall Tungsten Estimate
models.description: Rough proxy calculation: first-wall surface area x thickness = volume; volume x tungsten density = mass.

calculations.name: Tungsten volume
calculations.formula: Volume = First-Wall Area x First-Wall Thickness

calculations.name: Tungsten mass
calculations.formula: Tungsten Mass = Volume x Tungsten Density

models.name: ELMT Valuation Sensitivity Model
models.description: Illustrative sensitivity: if ELMT were valued at ~3x current equity value and investors required ~15x incremental EBITDA at a ~25% incremental margin, how much annual fusion revenue would that require? These are illustrative sensitivity calculations, not forecasts.

calculations.name: ELMT illustrative fusion revenue target
calculations.formula: Required Fusion Revenue = (Current Market Cap x 3 x (1/15)) / Incremental EBITDA Margin

scenarios.name: High-demand / constrained tritium
scenarios.description: Reactor demand accelerates, but tritium supply remains the binding constraint on near-term deployment pace.

scenarios.name: Fusion Bull
scenarios.description: Faster commercialization, successful pilot plants, high reactor deployment, strong component demand, rapid supplier scale-up.

scenarios.name: Fusion Delay
scenarios.description: Projects slip, revenue timing shifts later, valuations compress.

scenarios.name: Materials Bottleneck
scenarios.description: Tungsten or other structural material limits deployment; qualified suppliers gain pricing power.

scenarios.name: HTS Breakthrough
scenarios.description: Lower conductor cost, faster magnet deployment, increased HTS demand.

scenarios.name: Tritium Bottleneck
scenarios.description: Startup-inventory and extraction constraints delay deployment.

scenarios.name: Fusion False Dawn
scenarios.description: Impressive technical milestones, poor economics, commercialization fails to scale.

scenarios.name: Supplier Winner
scenarios.description: One supplier captures a disproportionate share; qualification/capacity creates a durable moat.

scenarios.name: Commodity Trap
scenarios.description: Commodity demand rises, but suppliers fail to capture meaningful economic value from it.
